name: Bank Albilad
legal_name: Bank Albilad (a Saudi Joint Stock Company)
founded: 2004 (Royal Decree 48/M dated 21/9/1425H, 4 Nov 2004). AR 2025: the Kingdom's 11th bank; original shareholders were 8 money-exchange houses, who contributed SAR 1.5bn, with the public paying another SAR 1.5bn.
ownership_summary: Listed Saudi Islamic bank with a family-led shareholder base. Three holders above 5% at 31 Dec 2025: Mohammed Ibrahim AlSubeaei & Sons Company (19.34%), Abdulrahman Al Rajhi Investment Fund Company (6.71%) and Abdullah Ibrahim AlSubeaei Investment Company (6.36%). Paid-up capital SAR 15bn after a 2025 increase from SAR 12.5bn.

shareholders.holder: Abdulrahman Al Rajhi Investment Fund Company

government_link: No government shareholder above 5% disclosed at 31 Dec 2025 (AR 2025 major shareholders page, S4).
group_structure: Parent bank with five subsidiaries that the interim FS say are directly or indirectly 100% owned: Albilad Investment Company (Albilad Capital; capital SAR 500m; profiled separately as sa-albilad-capital), Albilad Real Estate Company, Enjaz Payment Services Company (SAMA-licensed Major Electronic Money Institution), Financial Solutions Company for Investment and Dufaa Finance Company. The website also names Mukafaat Albilad (loyalty) and Horizon Center (financial innovation) as group companies. Double counting: Albilad Capital is consolidated and sits inside the bank's 'Investment banking and brokerage' segment (SAR 433.0m of operating income in FY2025, close to Albilad Capital's own FY2024 figure in sa-albilad-capital). Never add sa-albilad-capital figures to this record. The AR says the only financing to a subsidiary is Saudi National Bank's two short-term SAR 50m facilities to Albilad Capital.

footprint: Saudi Arabia only: 108 branches at end-2025 plus specialised SME centres, with no branches or companies operating abroad (AR 2025). Head office Al Mutamarat, Riyadh. FY2025 operating income by region: Central SAR 4,857m, Western 822m, Eastern 513m.
customer_segments: Retail (Awaed Albilad, Zood savings, Tamayuz Gold and Diamond tiers, personal and mortgage finance, cards), private banking and UHNW, SMEs (a stated strategic focus), corporate banking including funds and REITs and government bodies, treasury.
business_lines: Four reporting segments, FY2025 operating income (SAR m, share): Retail banking 2,410 (39%), Corporate banking 1,912 (31%), Treasury 1,437 (23%), Investment banking and brokerage 433 (7%; Albilad Capital). Retail covers deposits, financing (Bei-ajel, installment sales, Musharakah, Ijarah), remittances, cards and Private Banking. Fee income FY2025 included mutual fund and other management fees SAR 169.7m and brokerage income SAR 37.5m (group lines). Payments and remittances run through Enjaz.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Albilad is a Shariah-only retail and corporate bank whose wealth offer is thin at bank level. Affluent clients sit in the Tamayuz Gold and Diamond tiers (Diamond adds priority banking with a dedicated relationship manager; no eligibility thresholds or investment benefits are published), and Private Banking offers one-to-one service through a request form with no published thresholds. In 2025 Retail Banking added a Quick Financing Program for private-banking customers and executive-lounge and executive-office access for UHNW clients, and the AR cites 'enhanced offerings for affluent customer segments'. The only investment product in the new bank app is the Investment Wakalah account (from SAR 50,000 or USD 30,000, indicative profit up to about 5%). Securities, funds and ETFs sit in the 100%-owned Albilad Capital, which runs its own trading apps, 7 ETFs and mutual funds (see sa-albilad-capital); its segment was 7% of FY2025 operating income (SAR 433m) and fell 19% in H1 2026. A new CEO took over on 1 Jun 2026.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking page: 'tailored banking services', relationship management, centres, online request form. AR 2025: Quick Financing Program for private-banking customers; executive-lounge access for UHNW clients. No thresholds, investment products or head named; no private banking AUM disclosed.

asset_management.detail: Through Albilad Capital (100%): ETFs, public mutual funds, discretionary portfolios, real estate funds. AR 2025: ETF leadership above 70% local market share and about 53% regional share. Group management fees on mutual funds and others SAR 169.7m in FY2025. Details in sa-albilad-capital.

brokerage.detail: Through Albilad Capital: Saudi market and international trading; AR 2025 says 76% of trading turnover went through web and mobile. Group brokerage income line SAR 37.5m in FY2025 (SAR 61.7m in FY2024). Details in sa-albilad-capital.

digital_investing.detail: The new Albilad app (2025) opens an Investment (Wakala) account online but lists no funds, stocks or trading. Equity, ETF, fund and IPO investing is in Albilad Capital's separate apps (see sa-albilad-capital). An Investor Relations App launched alongside the new bank app is for shareholders.

advisory.detail: Relationship managers serve Tamayuz Diamond and Private Banking clients, but no investment advisory service, suitability process or advisory fee is published at bank level.

discretionary.detail: Albilad Capital lists Discretionary Portfolio Management; terms and minimums not published (see sa-albilad-capital). Nothing at bank level.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found on the bank site, in the app page or in AR 2025.

funds_platform.detail: No third-party fund shelf found. The bank site links to Albilad Capital for investments; Albilad Capital distributes its own funds.

structured_products.detail: No structured products or capital-protected notes found in the bank's retail, private banking pages or AR 2025.

private_markets.detail: Via Albilad Capital: real estate funds (2025 launches: Makkah Vision Real Estate Fund, Qurtubah Square, Hittin, Albilad Investment Opportunity Fund 2) and hospitality funds. See sa-albilad-capital.

islamic_wealth.detail: Whole bank is Shariah-compliant under a Shariah Committee: Investment Wakalah (Shariah Committee approved, zakat treatment explained), Awaed Albilad, Goal Saving; Albilad Capital sukuk ETF and Shariah-screened funds.

opportunities: Wealth is a gap at bank level: the bank app's only investment product is the Investment Wakalah account (minimum SAR 50,000 or USD 30,000), while funds and equities require Albilad Capital's separate apps (S14, S15, S4 PDF p.64)

AR 2025 cites 'enhanced offerings for affluent customer segments' and 2025 UHNW and private-banking additions, but the Private Banking page publishes no thresholds, products or advisory process (S4 PDF pp.15, 40-41; S13)
Tamayuz Diamond promises a dedicated relationship manager, yet no investment or wealth benefit is listed for Tamayuz tiers (S16)
The Investment banking and brokerage segment's H1 2026 operating income fell 19.4% year on year (SAR 189.1m vs 234.7m) and its pre-zakat income fell 35.2% (S7 PDF p.36)
New CEO from 1 Jun 2026, promoted from Senior Executive Vice President, Businesses, so the retail and wealth agenda may be reset (S9, S10, S11)
Retail growth is led by mortgages, personal finance and cards; investment income is small (SAR 433m of SAR 6,192m, 7%) (S4 PDF p.34)
barriers: Wealth products and licences sit in Albilad Capital, a separate CMA-licensed subsidiary with its own apps, ETF franchise and partners (S3, S4 PDF p.63)
Shariah-only bank: every product needs Shariah Committee approval (S7 note 1b)
Stated strategy emphasises sustainable growth, SME Islamic banking and digital leadership; wealth is not named as a pillar in the AR strategy review (S4 PDF p.11)
Chair and CEO both changed on 1 Jun 2026, and no head of wealth, private banking or digital is named on the website or AR 2025 (S1, S2, S4)
Intellect eMACH.ai chosen for wholesale banking in 2025 shows a preference for a single strategic platform vendor on the corporate side (S19)
